notes: Shared by every mobile platform's notification code; see docs/adr/0002-notification-message-text.md.
input is a message's content; expected is the notification body shown for it.
Lengths are in UTF-16 code units: the body is at most 256, including the ellipsis.

cases.name: plain text is unchanged
links show their text, bare URLs stay
mention links show the name
images show their alt text
fenced code keeps its text and line breaks, drops the fence and language
cases.input:
Try this:
```swift
let x = 1
  print(x)
```
Then run it.
cases.expected:
Try this:
let x = 1
  print(x)
Then run it.

cases.name: single-line fenced code keeps its text
backticks inside a fenced block don't close it
a closing fence at the end of the last code line closes the block
a block fenced with four backticks keeps its code
a four-backtick block can hold a three-backtick fence
an unclosed fence on one line runs to the end of the text
a block's opening line is dropped even when it has a backtick
inline code keeps its text
bold and strikethrough markers are removed
Markdown inside code is left alone
a combining mark next to a code span's backticks is kept
single asterisks, underscores, quotes, lists and headings stay as typed
runs of spaces collapse outside code, trailing spaces are removed
CRLF becomes LF and three or more line breaks become one blank line
leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed
a message that is only whitespace is empty
exactly 256 UTF-16 units is unchanged
257 UTF-16 units becomes 255 plus an ellipsis
the cap counts UTF-16 units and never splits a character
whitespace before the ellipsis is trimmed
a link label can contain inline code
a link label can mix text and code
image alt text can be code
bold and strikethrough can wrap code
markup inside code stays literal
an unclosed fence runs to the end
content past 4096 units is dropped and marked with an ellipsis
a fenced block cut at 4096 units keeps its code text
